text:
Ana: Quick sync - we need a decision on what to trim from the April milestone so we can keep the MVP date. Options below.
Devon: listing the options please.
Ana: TL;DR: keep core inference runtime + API, ship a minimal model-pinning surface (pin by model id only), drop the full pin-management UI to v1, and defer detailed route-level telemetry retention to v1.
Kai: +1 on minimal pin surface. Engineering risk for pin UI is larger than people think. Backend pin proto is done, UI is nontrivial.
Raj: Customers that asked for pinning care about rolling back pins quickly. Can we do a bare-bones rollback endpoint and a CLI tool instead of full UI?
Devon: Yes — we can expose POST /pins/rollbacks and add a small CLI wrapper. That cuts ~2 sprint-weeks from frontend.
Marie: Design note: If we do CLI first, we should still ship a tiny in-console header that shows current pinned model and a link to the CLI instructions. Keeps UX readable for pilots.
Ana: Good call. So propose: MVP = API + runtime + minimal pin API + CLI + tiny console header. Cut = full pin-management UI, advanced tag filters, and route-level telemetry long retention.
Kai: What about the embeddings-eviction cache dashboard? That was on the nice-to-have list.
Ana: Cut that from MVP — keep backend cache and metrics exposed via /metrics only. Dashboard -> v1.
Devon: Impact on customers? Any paying pilot that explicitly needs the dashboard?
Raj: Two pilots asked for dashboards. Both said dashboard is nice, not blocking. They want predictable latency and easy rollback.
Marie: We should keep an onboarding checklist in the console that points to how to enable predictable latency policies (autoscale + routing policies). That’s higher impact than a detailed cache dashboard.
Ana: Agree. Also, we should keep the canary rollout mechanism — that’s critical for safety. Small UI: toggle + % slider; advanced rollout flows to v1.
Devon: Canary core is implemented in routing layer; adding the console toggle is one frontend sprint. OK.
Kai: Anything else on the cutlist? We still have the "quality monitoring regression alerting tied to prompt sets" feature — heavy infra.
Ana: Cut that. MVP will have manual evals + a simple alerts webhook (teams can wire their own). Full eval suite -> v1.
Raj: Are we comfortable with this for the April milestone? Dev capacity looks tight but doable with these cuts.
Devon: With UI cuts, yes. We'll reallocate 2 FE sprints to runtime perf and canary safety tests.
Marie: I'll draft the console copy for the header and onboarding checklist today.
Ana: Action items: Devon — confirm sprint estimates for CLI + header + toggle by EOD. Kai — validate that rollback endpoint + canary tests satisfy pilot SLAs. Marie — draft console copy & CLI doc. Raj — notify pilots about scope trade and get thumbs up. I'll update the milestone tracker.
Devon: estimate: CLI + header + toggle = 10 dev-days. Canary safety tests = 6 dev-days. Rollback endpoint = 4 dev-days. Total 20 dev-days.
Kai: SLA validation: I can run a lightweight runbook to show rollback < 3 mins and canary fallback under 500ms added latency. Will confirm by tomorrow.
Raj: I'll ping the pilots now: @acme_pilot and @greenleaf_pilot.
release-bot: Note: the April milestone freeze is in 9 business days. Last build cutoff: 1763805400.
Ana: Thanks — aim to lock scope by EOD tomorrow. If pilots push back, we'll re-evaluate but prefer shipping minimal safe surface.
Marie: small UX concern — header copy needs to be clear about "pinned models are global to tenant". I'll include that.
Devon: one more: we should document the rollback audit trail in logs (request id + actor). Low effort and high confidence for audits.
Ana: Add that to the list. Ok team — I'll update the tracker and mark the UI parts as v1 backlog.
Raj: thumbs up from me.
Kai: thumbs up.
Marie: :thumbsup:
Devon: :shipit: 
Ana: Closing — will post updated milestone entry once tracker is updated.
